nodes.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the restriction of $f$ to the empty set, that is, the sum of the terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\emptyset$, is the zero polynomial.
nodes.title: Edge restriction to the empty set

nodes.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the restriction of $f$ to all of $\mathbb{R}^2$, that is, the sum of the terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\mathbb{R}^2$, is $f$ itself.
nodes.title: Edge restriction to the whole plane

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, and let $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. The restriction of $f$ to $\Gamma$ is the polynomial formed by the terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\Gamma$; the other terms are dropped.
nodes.title: Restriction of a polynomial to a set of exponents

nodes.summary: The map from exponent vectors of monomials in two variables to $\mathbb{R}^2$ sends $e = (e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ to the point $(e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Exponent vectors as points of the plane

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$. A point $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$ lies in the Newton support of $f$ if and only if $x$ is the exponent vector $e \in \mathbb{N}^2$ of some monomial with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Membership in the Newton support

nodes.summary: For a polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the boundary of the Newton polygon of $f$ is its topological boundary in $\mathbb{R}^2$: the closure of the Newton polygon minus its interior.
nodes.title: Boundary of the Newton polygon

nodes.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the interior of the Newton polygon of $f$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is contained in the Newton polygon of $f$.
nodes.title: The interior of the Newton polygon lies in the polygon

nodes.summary: For a polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the interior of the Newton polygon of $f$ is its topological interior as a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Interior of the Newton polygon

nodes.summary: For every commutative semiring $k$, the Newton polygon of the zero polynomial in two variables over $k$ is the empty subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: The Newton polygon of the zero polynomial is empty

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$. The Newton polygon of $f$ is the convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^2$ of the Newton support of $f$, the set of exponent vectors of the monomials with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as points of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Newton polygon

nodes.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the Newton support of $f$ is contained in the Newton polygon of $f$, the convex hull of the Newton support in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: The Newton support lies in the Newton polygon

nodes.summary: For every commutative semiring $k$, the Newton support of the zero polynomial in two variables over $k$ is the empty subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: The Newton support of the zero polynomial is empty

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables $x_0, x_1$ over a commutative semiring $k$. The Newton support of $f$ is the set of exponent vectors $(e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ of the monomials $x_0^{e_0} x_1^{e_1}$ with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as points of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Newton support

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
